More visibility for workingDirectories setting
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. This still looks like a useful configuration-discoverability improvement. Current main supports `eslint.workingDirectories`, including `mode: auto`, explicit directories, and patterns, but it does not detect a likely nested-project mismatch and offer that configuration to the user. The safer direction remains the one discussed here: retain the current default, scan conservatively for likely monorepo layouts, and present a user-confirmed settings recommendation rather than changing behavior automatically.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the detailed follow-up. This was addressed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/d8214448aa1ba338c84184239bfee66cea24fbaa: failures from `fs.realpathSync.native` are now caught and the server falls back to the original file path instead of letting the exception interrupt linting. The fix first shipped in the 2.4.1 pre-release and is included in stable 2.4.2 and later, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in release/2.4.2.

rows.title: Reporting errors from node_module and no way to suppress/disable (also ignores .eslintignore)`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and reproduction. The command-line result confirms that this error comes from legacy ESLint config resolution: ESLint attempts to load the dependency's `eslintConfig` before it can determine that the file is ignored. That behavior was confirmed upstream in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/14686, although ESLint declined to change the frozen eslintrc implementation. The extension delegates both config and ignore resolution to the workspace-installed ESLint, and `eslint.onIgnoredFiles` only controls warnings after ESLint successfully identifies a file as ignored; it cannot suppress this configuration-loading failure.

rows.title: Prefer to use node from environment
Feature Request: enable the "eslint.format.enable" setting by default.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. `eslint.format.enable` is intentionally opt-in because VS Code can use different formatters for the same language. Enabling ESLint's formatter for everyone would make it compete with choices such as the TypeScript or Prettier formatter and would be a breaking change for users relying on the current default. If ESLint should format a language, enable `eslint.format.enable` and set `editor.defaultFormatter` for that language to `dbaeumer.vscode-eslint`; for fix-on-save behavior, `editor.codeActionsOnSave` with `source.fixAll.eslint` is the more configurable option. Given those compatibility constraints, the current default is working as designed.

rows.title: A change to eslint.debug requires VSCode restart if the ESLint server was already running
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and confirmations. The manual restart should apply the current `eslint.debug` value, but current main computes the server process environment only when the language client is first created; the normal `ESLint: Restart ESLint Server` path reuses that client and its stale launch options. Keeping this open as a bug. The fix should recompute the process-launch settings during restart; whether changing `eslint.debug` should also trigger an automatic restart can be considered separately.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for following up. The enable/disable commands were intentionally removed in favor of VS Code's Extension panel, as explained in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1172#issuecomment-772377513. Since VS Code can now disable and re-enable the extension without requiring a restart, the original friction is addressed by that standard platform surface, so closing this as working as designed.

rows.title: Extension can't find typescript-eslint parser with yarn's pnpm linker installation layout
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for clarifying the distinction from Yarn PnP. Current `main` still uses the parser's resolved path to recognize TypeScript support for legacy configurations, and the Yarn pnpm-linker virtual-store path does not match those checks. ESLint 9 flat config takes a newer path that enables validation when a matching config is returned, but that does not establish that the legacy-layout gap is fixed. Keeping this open to track package-layout-independent probing; in the meantime, `eslint.validate` with `typescript` and `typescriptreact` remains the supported workaround.

rows.title: Feature request: Provide a way to control files fixed during onCodeActionsSave (e.g., ignorePatterns)
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the request. This is now supported by `eslint.codeActionsOnSave.options`, added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/6f8769b072debf9ac124b55893dbc19e1bf8795d and first shipped in the 3.0.15 pre-release (stable in 3.0.16). For example:

```json
"eslint.codeActionsOnSave.options": {
  "ignorePatterns": ["**/*.md", "**/*.mdx"]
}
```

These options are applied specifically when ESLint computes fixes on save, so normal validation can continue using the workspace's regular configuration. Closing as implemented. The fix shipped in release/3.0.16.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the follow-up and for fixing the client-side capability filtering in https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/14666. The server still reads only the first entry in `context.only`, so keeping this in the backlog as a defensive interoperability improvement makes sense: it should consider all requested kinds and avoid returning ESLint quick fixes under an unsupported kind, while clients should continue filtering requests against the advertised capabilities for performance.

rows.title: Support for `typescript-eslint` v8's parser `projectService`
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed reproduction and follow-up reports. This is a projectService-specific instance of the broader cross-file invalidation problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1774, which covers how the extension should communicate filesystem changes or refresh long-lived ESLint state without an expensive blanket restart.

The typescript-eslint 8.3.0 mitigation handles some newly created files, but the reports here on 8.7.0 and on creating a new folder before its first file show that it does not cover the full problem. Those projectService-specific details and the NX reproduction should be carried into the canonical issue. Closing this report as a duplicate so the remaining watcher and invalidation design stays consolidated there.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional reproduction work. The key distinction appears to be how dependencies are installed: Codespaces initially installs this repository with npm, which masks the problem, while removing `node_modules` and running `pnpm install` reproduces the plugin-resolution failure even though `pnpm eslint` succeeds. The reproduction at https://github.com/angryermine/vscode-eslint-pnpm and the logs in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1986#issuecomment-3630973937 give us a concrete pnpm 10 case to investigate, so this should remain open.

rows.title: respect estlint-suppressions.json
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request and the follow-up context. Bulk-suppression support has now shipped in the stable 3.0.34 release. Enable it with `eslint.bulkSuppression.enable`; `eslint.bulkSuppression.location` can select a non-default suppression file, and `eslint.bulkSuppression.severity` controls how suppressed violations appear, including `hint`. This requires ESLint 10.1 or newer. The implementation is in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/9d33f02b2ddaadc55f7f30dfd2338ccca12dc798. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.

rows.title: Loading flat config from the node_modules fails
Measure rule performance through VSCode ESLint
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed request. Setting `eslint.options.stats` should already pass `stats: true` to the workspace ESLint constructor, but the server currently reads diagnostics from the returned lint result and does not consume its `stats` property. Since the extension uses ESLint's Node.js API rather than launching its CLI, an executable wrapper is not the right integration point; `eslint.runtime` controls the Node runtime used for the language server, not an ESLint executable. A focused implementation could read `LintResult.stats` in the server validation path and log an opt-in timing summary to the ESLint output channel without requiring an additional client/server protocol message.

rows.title: VS Code ESLint@3.0.16 --debug option
FEAT: Use ESLint extension without auto run
Server side workingDirectory.mode auto detection is incomplete
multithreaded/--concurrency support?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional graphql-eslint context. The server currently validates each document through ESLint's `lintText` API, while ESLint's concurrency feature is designed to distribute multiple target files across workers. `eslint.options` can already pass constructor options through to ESLint, but setting `concurrency` alone would not create a useful multi-file workload in the current validation path. Keeping this request open to investigate and benchmark whether pending validations can be safely batched without making normal single-file validation slower.

rows.title: Extension should report config file errors
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The extension currently records an unrecognized validation failure in the `ESLint` output channel and marks the ESLint language status as an error, but the flat-config `InvalidConfigError` path is not recognized by the more visible configuration-error handling. Keeping this open to track an actionable notification and, where ESLint provides a reliable source location, a diagnostic on the relevant `eslint.config.*` file.

rows.title: Request: add quick-fix action for adding same-line disables, i.e. `// eslint-disable-line`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. `eslint.codeAction.disableRuleComment.location` does support choosing `"sameLine"` globally, which is a useful workaround. The remaining request here is different: expose both same-line and separate-line quick fixes for each diagnostic so the choice can be made contextually without changing the setting. That is also distinct from the automatic JSX/TSX detection tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1074, so this should remain open as a feature request.

rows.title: /* eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars */  will disappear when save
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for providing the sample. I still need this as a minimal GitHub repository that can be cloned so the ESLint dependencies and configuration can be inspected unchanged. Please also include the `.vscode/settings.json`, the workspace's ESLint version, and the `ESLint` output-channel content from a save that removes the comment. In particular, please show whether the diagnostic is from `no-unused-vars` or `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` and whether `eslint.codeActionsOnSave.rules` is configured; restricting the rules used during save can make ESLint consider a directive unused and remove it.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. To investigate this, please provide the minimal GitHub repository requested above, including the ESLint configuration and the file that demonstrates the problem. Please also include the `ESLint` output channel contents and the workspace ESLint, extension, and VS Code versions. rows.title: docs: Document for `eslint.lintTask.command` is missing
ESLint plugin breaks when using `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional detail. This now has a concrete task-specific reproduction: enable `eslint.lintTask.enable`, set `eslint.lintTask.command` to `yarn eslint`, and run `eslint: lint whole folder` in the provided repository without opening a file first. Per-file validation uses ESLint's structured results and works, while the task sends stylish CLI output through VS Code's `$eslint-stylish` problem matcher; that matcher is line-oriented, so multiline react-hooks messages prevent later diagnostics from being recognized. This should stay open while we determine whether the core matcher needs to support multiline messages or the lint task should use a different output path.

rows.title: Eslint client couldn't create connection to server after installing new VS Code version

rows.title: ESLint version 10.0.3 only supports flat configs. Setting is ignored
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and investigation. This was a spurious message caused by the extension forwarding the default value of `eslint.experimental.useFlatConfig` even when that setting was not configured. It was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/5a2809ce452e41c84747b86a0334734e87e9c87b and first shipped in pre-release version 3.0.25; the fix is also included in the current 3.0.34 release. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.

rows.title: Extension causes high cpu load

A minimal GitHub repository that reproduces the high CPU usage, along with the `ESLint` output-channel contents while it occurs, would also help distinguish extension overhead from workspace configuration, ESLint, or a plugin.
